selected.quote: And you know she had no other choice, I mean, it was either this or Juvie Hall. I mean, you just can't keep moving away every time you get into trouble.
selected.justification: angle.md names B17 in prose as "the exact words the thesis pays off", and this span is those words with nothing else in them - so the sentence the whole recap then spends sixteen minutes testing is planted by the character who says it, not by the narrator paraphrasing him.
selected.self_contained: Everything the quote leans on is already in the draft before 897.88s. "Juvie Hall": line 13 established two priors, strike three, and "prison, unless there's another way". "She" has a referent: his mother speaks in line 14 and is the subject of line 15, and the rewritten line 17 puts her back in the frame one sentence before the hand-over. "You just can't keep moving away every time you get into trouble" lands against line 15's "Every time he loses, an adult relocates him" - the narrator has given the viewer the pattern, and this is the first character to name it. No name, relationship or plot fact in the quote is unintroduced; the speaker's identity is established by the rewritten line 17 immediately before it.

before.new_narration: The next thing Sean knows he is in Tokyo, in a cramped one-room flat with a father he has barely seen - a US Navy officer posted here, suddenly a near-stranger with custody of him. His mother is an ocean away. The man has clearly been rehearsing this one. Listen.
before.why: Line 17 as written IS the paraphrase - it says "this stay is the only thing standing between him and juvenile hall, and you cannot keep running every single time trouble finds you", which is both halves of the quote in the narrator's mouth, and it is where narration_overlap 0.38 comes from. The rewrite keeps line 17's job (ocean crossed, who the man is, the one-room flat per B17) and ends by turning the floor over to him, while saying none of the three things the quote says: not the mother's lack of choice, not this-or-juvenile-hall, not the running. It keeps the mother on screen so "she" has an antecedent four seconds later. Original 55 words, replacement 49.

after.new_narration: Hold onto that line. Then come the three rules - school, straight home, nowhere near a car - from a man with no standing to enforce any of them.
after.why: Reacts rather than restates: it flags the sentence as load-bearing (the draft's own running-bit device, moved from line 17 to after the hand-over where it now belongs) and then says what the line is worth by pointing at who said it - a man with no standing. It does not repeat the words that just played. Line 18's own payload is preserved intact: the three rules of B18, which lines 31-32 and 45 pay off. Original 26 words, replacement 27.

selected.quote: Don't argue with me. I did this. I can't run away.
selected.justification: It is the turn the angle is built on - the first time Sean refuses to be relocated out of his own trouble - and it answers the act-one hand-over almost word for word, so the film states the diagnosis and the cure in its own voice at both ends of the recap.
selected.self_contained: The viewer has the pattern from both directions by now: narration in line 15 ("Every time he loses, an adult relocates him") and the film's own voice in pick 1. "I did this" needs no antecedent - lines 71 to 76 just showed Sean in the chase and sprinting at the burning wreck, so the viewer knows exactly what "this" is and that R2 has landed. The father is established as a presence in the scene by line 77 ("until his father draws") and as the rule-setter by lines 17-18 and 32. "I can't run away" is the only phrase that carries weight, and it is the phrase the recap has been teaching since line 14.

before.new_narration: In the alley his father tries to take the whole thing off his hands - his mess to answer for, his boy to get out of Tokyo. Every other time in Sean's life, an adult decided what happened next. Listen to him now.
before.why: Line 79 as written quotes the beat outright - "I did this, he says. I can't run away from it" - which is the narration_overlap of 0.60 on this candidate and 1.00 on the 4665.3 variant. The rewrite gives only the father's side (B83's responsibility claim, B84's press to leave Tokyo, both inside or adjacent to line 79's clip window) and recalls the running bit, then stops. Sean's answer is left entirely to the film. It also drops line 79's closing verdict "The first time Sean refuses to be moved on", which is moved to the after line where it is a reaction instead of a spoiler. Original 40 words, replacement 42.

after.new_narration: That is the first time in his life he refuses to be moved on. So he tells Twinkie he is walking into Kamata's house himself. Twinkie calls it suicide.
after.why: Tells the viewer what it meant rather than what was said: the refusal is the hinge of the angle, and the cost of it is the next sentence - having refused the only exit on offer, he has to go at Kamata himself. Line 80's B86 payload is kept and the hand-off into line 81 ("That's all I've got.") still reads as Sean's reply, now cued by "Twinkie calls it suicide", which is B86's own wording. Original 29 words, replacement 29.

The arithmetic that kills the obvious third: the act 4 candidates that pass audio are 4769.08 and 4780.54, and 4769.08 - 4664.22 = 104.86s and 4780.54 - 4664.22 = 116.32s, both < 180, so neither can sit beside pick 2. count_note: Two, not three, and this is not a shortfall of judgement - it is what the measurements leave. Act 2 contributes nothing eligible: the 2236-2251 Han deal family passes audio at 4.0-4.9 dB but fails rule a on inspection (the 0.67 match against "I don't drift to win" is overlap on I/don't/drift; the span states a bargain, not the angle), the 2520-2533 B48 exchange is the genuine thesis-adjacent line there and measures 2.2-2.3 dB, 0.7 dB short, and the rest of act 2 is garbled transcript or crowd noise. Act 4 contributes nothing usable: everything past the 180s line from pick 2 measures 1.8 dB or negative, including the climax line at 1.6 and -1.8 dB, and the two spans that are clean (4769.08, 4780.54) are inside 117s of pick 2 and fail rule a as well. So a third pick would have to break spacing, overrule a measurement, or hand the film's only voice to a line that means nothing. Two strong ones beat that. What the two are worth: they are the same sentence said twice, once by the man who diagnoses the pattern in act 1 and once by the boy who finally breaks it in act 3 - the angle's spine, in the film's own voice, at both ends of the recap.
